Twiglet: Holds so still that birds perch on it. It finds this insulting.
Phasmark: Sways with a wind only it can feel, one step ahead of every blow.
Phasmarch: A whole thicket that walks. Travellers count the trees twice.
Acornet: Rolls downhill by accident and uphill out of spite.
Quercor: Its bark records every storm it has stood through.
Oakwarden: Villages are planted in its shade and ask its leave to build.
Dionasnap: Its jaws close faster than the spark that triggers them.
Flytyrant: Lightning bends toward it, as if called home for supper.
Glowfly: Blinks in a pattern the others pretend to understand.
Luminfly: Hangs over water to admire a light it thinks is someone else.
Lampyra: Lost hikers follow it. Some are led home.
Sparkant: Carries embers the way other ants carry crumbs.
Scaldant: Marches in lines that leave the ground too hot to cross.
Ignisregina: Her colony is a furnace, and she is its only door.
Komodle: Tastes the air for anything warm, then bites that.
Varanox: Its patience is the most dangerous thing about it.
Komodrake: Old enough that the island's volcano is named after it.
Blowpuff: Swells at loud noises, its own included.
Spikepuff: Drifts where it likes; the tide has learned to go around.
Tetrablast: Exhales, and the reef rearranges itself.
Whalelet: Sings one note, badly, and is very proud of it.
Balaenor: Its song is felt in the ribs before it is heard.
Abyssalon: Sleeps under the waves; storms are it turning over.
Latrolet: Spins more web than it needs and sits in the middle, pleased.
Latrovane: Reads the wind through its threads and is never surprised.
Latrowidow: Every strand in the hollow leads back to her.
Grimlarva: Eats by night and squeaks when the moon looks at it.
Acheromoth: The mark on its back is a face. It is not its own.
Atroposphinx: Where its wings pass, lamps gutter and dogs fall quiet.
Hummlet: Too fast to see clearly, too curious to stay away.
Trochilume: Its wings hum a chord that makes flowers open.
Hovermarch: Flies the whole coast each spring without touching ground.
Fluffseed: Goes wherever the wind does and calls it a plan.
Taraxwisp: Sheds seeds like a held breath let go.
Taraxstorm: A meadow's worth of seed, turning in one slow gale.
